Comment: First cortical processing area for visual information. Extracts visual features of numbers and mathematical formulas. (Outside ROI - input only)
Output Semantics: Luminance contrast in retinal coordinates; edge orientation; spatial frequency

Comment: Second stage of early visual processing. Processes basic visual features such as color and shape. (Outside ROI - input)
Output Semantics: Integrated representation of color; shape; texture and other early visual features

Comment: Shape processing and motion detection. Intermediate-level visual processing. (Outside ROI - input)
Higher-order processing of color and shape. Pre-stage of object recognition. (Outside ROI - input)
Output Semantics: Integrated representation of object color and complex shape features

Comment: Posterior region of IPS (including IPS0-2, hIP1). Forms initial representations of visually presented numbers and quantities. Integration of visuospatial and numerical information. (Inside ROI)
Output Semantics: Magnitude relationships and spatial arrangement of visually presented quantities. Visuospatial representation of numbers.
Requirement: To realize the TLF 'Mathematical knowledge', it is necessary to extract the numerical aspect from visually presented mathematical information (numbers, formulas) and represent magnitude relationships and spatial arrangements. Input: Receives visual features from [U.V2][U.V3][U.V4] and semantic information of numbers from [U.FG-math]. Output: Sends quantity representation to [U.aIPS] and feedback to [U.FG-math]. Receives top-down control signals from [U.dlPFC][U.ACC], episodic memory from [U.Hippocampus], reward signals from [U.Striatum], and syntactic information from [U.Broca].
Requirement realization by interface: Realized through interface ([U.aIPS], [U.FG-math], [U.Pulvinar], [U.ACC], [U.Striatum]) = U.pIPS([U.V2], [U.V3], [U.V4], [U.FG-math], [U.aIPS], [U.dlPFC], [U.Pulvinar], [U.ACC], [U.Hippocampus], [U.Striatum], [U.Broca]). Integrates visual features from visual areas [U.V2][U.V3][U.V4] with number form information from [U.FG-math] to form quantity representations and outputs to [U.aIPS]. Attention is selectively allocated by control signals from [U.dlPFC] and [U.ACC].
Capability: Ability to extract numerosity from a visually presented stimulus set. Encodes magnitude relationships while preserving visuospatial arrangement information. This capacity is implemented as an Approximate Number System (ANS) following the Weber-Fechner law (Dehaene, 2011). At the single-neuron level, numerosity tuning curves showing preference for specific numerosities are observed (Nieder & Miller, 2004; Harvey et al., 2013).
Mechanism: Encoding by neuronal populations with numerosity tuning. From visual input, a location map is constructed; summation clusters form monotonic tuning; then neurons with unimodal numerosity tuning are generated through central excitation and lateral inhibition (Dehaene & Changeux, 1993). As numerosity increases, tuning curve width broadens, explaining behavioral characteristics observed as the Weber-Fechner law (Piazza et al., 2004).
Implementation: [U.pIPS] = Σ(Gaussian([U.V2], [U.V3], [U.V4]) * w_visual) + [U.FG-math] * w_semantic - Lateral_inhibition([U.pIPS_neighbors]) + [U.dlPFC] * w_attention + [U.ACC] * w_control

Comment: Anterior region of IPS (including IPS3-4, hIP2-3). Representation of abstract numerical relationships and mathematical reasoning. Supports quantity operations in working memory through collaboration with prefrontal cortex. (Inside ROI)
Output Semantics: Abstract quantity relationships; numerical ordinality; intermediate results of mathematical reasoning. Sensory modality-independent quantity representation.
Requirement: To realize the TLF, it is necessary to transform the visual quantity representation formed in U.pIPS into abstract numerical relationships independent of sensory modality. Input: Receives visual quantity representation from [U.pIPS] and retrieved arithmetic facts from [U.AG]. Output: Sends feedback to [U.pIPS], quantity information to [U.AG], working memory transfer to [U.LIPFC], and motor planning to [U.PMC]. Receives control signals from [U.dlPFC][U.ACC], contextual information from [U.Hippocampus][U.Striatum], and syntactic information from [U.Broca].
Requirement realization by interface: Realized through interface ([U.pIPS], [U.AG], [U.LIPFC], [U.ACC], [U.Striatum], [U.PMC]) = U.aIPS([U.pIPS], [U.AG], [U.dlPFC], [U.ACC], [U.Hippocampus], [U.Striatum], [U.Broca]). Abstracts visual quantity representation from [U.pIPS] and integrates with arithmetic knowledge through interaction with [U.AG]. Working memory control from [U.dlPFC] supports quantity operations.
Capability: Ability to form abstract numerical representations independent of sensory modalities (visual, auditory, tactile, etc.) and support numerical ordinality, magnitude relationships, and mathematical reasoning. This capacity is conceptualized as the mental number line and observed behaviorally as spatial representation of numbers (SNARC effect) (Dehaene et al., 1993). Represents numerical relationships fundamental to arithmetic, such as numerical comparison and conceptual understanding of addition/subtraction (Arsalidou & Taylor, 2011).
Mechanism: Abstract encoding of numerosity is realized by neuronal populations that remove sensory details from visual representations and encode numerosity itself. Top-down signals from prefrontal cortex enable quantities to be maintained and manipulated in working memory. Numerical ordinality is realized through relative magnitude coding in frontoparietal networks (Harvey et al., 2024).
Implementation: [U.aIPS] = Abstract([U.pIPS]) + [U.AG] * w_fact + [U.dlPFC] * w_WM + [U.Hippocampus] * w_context, where Abstract(x) is a mapping that removes sensory details

Comment: Mathematical processing area of the fusiform gyrus. Visual recognition of number forms and maintains semantic representations of mathematical concepts. Responds specifically to mathematical content. (Inside ROI)
Output Semantics: Number form recognition; visual identity of mathematical symbols; number-semantic correspondence.
Requirement: To realize the TLF, it is necessary to recognize the forms of visually presented numbers and mathematical symbols and link them to semantic representations. Input: Receives higher-order visual features from [U.V4], quantity information from [U.pIPS], and concept information from [U.ITG-math]. Output: Sends number-semantic correspondence to [U.pIPS] and visual identity to [U.ITG-math]. Receives attention control from [U.dlPFC] and linguistic mathematical information from [U.Wernicke].
Requirement realization by interface: Realized through interface ([U.pIPS], [U.ITG-math]) = U.FG-math([U.V4], [U.pIPS], [U.ITG-math], [U.dlPFC], [U.Wernicke]). Recognizes visual features from [U.V4] as number forms and integrates with quantity representations from [U.pIPS] and conceptual representations from [U.ITG-math].
Capability: Ability to recognize forms of visually presented numbers (Arabic numerals, Roman numerals, etc.) and mathematical symbols (+, -, =, ∫, etc.) and link them to corresponding semantic representations. This functions as the Number Form Area, a numerical version of the Visual Word Form Area (VWFA) (Grotheer et al., 2016, 2018). Preference for mathematical processing takes priority over mere visual recognition of numbers (Grotheer et al., 2018).
Mechanism: Extracts visual identity of numbers from visual features (arrangement of line segments, curves, etc.) and links it to semantic representations within ventral temporal cortex. As the final stage of hierarchical visual processing, applies general mechanisms of object recognition (receptive field integration, invariance acquisition) to numbers and symbols.

Comment: Mathematical processing area of the inferior temporal gyrus. Maintains high-order semantic representations of mathematical concepts (e.g., abstract concepts such as "prime numbers," "periodicity"). Language-independent semantic memory of mathematical knowledge. (Inside ROI)
Output Semantics: Semantic content of mathematical concepts (e.g., primality, periodicity, symmetry, etc.); semantic representations of mathematical facts; mathematical categories.
Requirement: To realize the TLF, it is necessary to maintain high-order semantic representations of mathematical concepts and form semantic memory of mathematical knowledge independent of language. For example, representing abstract mathematical categories and concepts such as "prime numbers," "periodicity," and "symmetry." Input: Receives visual features from [U.V4], number forms from [U.FG-math], retrieved facts from [U.AG], control signals from [U.dlPFC], and linguistic concepts from [U.Wernicke]. Output: Sends feedback to [U.FG-math], concept representations to [U.AG], working memory transfer to [U.LIPFC], and motor planning to [U.PMC].
Requirement realization by interface: Realized through interface ([U.FG-math], [U.AG], [U.LIPFC], [U.PMC]) = U.ITG-math([U.V4], [U.FG-math], [U.AG], [U.dlPFC], [U.Wernicke]). Receives visual-semantic integration information from [U.FG-math] to form abstract mathematical concepts. Through interaction with [U.AG], concepts and facts are integrated.
Capability: Semantic categorization and maintenance of abstract representations of mathematical concepts. Encodes mathematical domains (arithmetic, algebra, geometry, calculus, etc.) and mathematical properties (primality, periodicity, symmetry, continuity, etc.). This representation is language-independent and activates during mathematical reflection while skipping language areas (Amalric & Dehaene, 2016, 2018). Organized based on semantic distance, with similar concepts represented adjacently (Amalric & Dehaene, 2018).
Mechanism: Applies general semantic memory mechanisms of ventral temporal cortex to mathematical concepts. Forms hierarchical category structures and organizes concepts at different levels of abstraction (concrete numbers → mathematical properties → mathematical domains). Organization of neural representations based on semantic similarity enables generalization between related concepts.

Comment: Mediates retrieval of arithmetic facts and recall of mathematical memory. Supports explicit retrieval of mathematical knowledge as part of the semantic memory system. (Outside ROI - output)
Output Semantics: Retrieved arithmetic facts (e.g. 7×8=56); explicit recall of mathematical memory

Comment: Maintenance of working memory and sending control signals. Top-down control supporting retrieval and manipulation of mathematical knowledge. (Outside ROI - input/output)
Output Semantics: Top-down control signals; selective allocation of attention; retrieval control signals

Comment: Supports retrieval of declarative mathematical facts. Transfer of mathematical information to working memory. (Outside ROI - output)
Modulation of visual attention and control of input to IPS. (Outside ROI - input)
Output Semantics: Visual attention modulation signals; salience map

Comment: Cognitive control and task performance monitoring. Control signals during retrieval of mathematical knowledge. (Outside ROI - input/output)
Output Semantics: Cognitive control signals; error detection; task-switching signals

Comment: Provides episodic memory and contextual information about mathematical facts. Involved in memory formation during learning. (Outside ROI - input)
Output Semantics: Episodic memory; contextual information; memory trace formation signals during learning

Comment: Provides reward and learning-related signals. Reinforcement learning in acquiring mathematical knowledge. (Outside ROI - input/output)
Output Semantics: Reward prediction error; reinforcement learning signals

Comment: Syntactic parsing of mathematical statements (linguistic structure only; not mathematical content). (Outside ROI - input)
Output Semantics: Syntactic structure information (grammatical parsing of mathematical statements); syntactic processing of quantifiers and logical operators

Comment: Processing of linguistic mathematical concepts. Understanding of mathematical information presented verbally. (Outside ROI - input)
Output Semantics: Linguistic mathematical concepts; semantic content of mathematical information presented verbally

Comment: Motor planning for mathematical responses (e.g., preparation for speaking or writing answers). (Outside ROI - output)
